newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down on Gresik's poor H1 net.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down on Gresik's poor H1 net.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended lower on Monday following selling pressure in Semen Gresik, one of the biggest capitalised stocks on the market, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 3.06 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 718.71 points. Decliners led advancers by 79 to 40 with 77 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 470 billion rupiah.
"Semen Gresik's worse than expected first half results have dragged overall market sentiment down," one broker said.
Semen Gresik posted a net profit of 87.37 billion rupiah in the first six months of 1997 against 115.65 billion rupiah in the same period of last year.
"We had expected it to post net profit of 106 billion rupiah for the first half," William Keeling, head of research with brokerage firm Kleinwort Benson said.

Keeling said he had recommended a sell for the state-controlled cement giant two years ago because of high financing costs due to the firm's capacity expansion and poor distribution network in key regions such as central and west Java.
"The poor results were due to the firm's failure to achieve high utilisation rate for its new plants," John Rachmat, an analyst with Schroders Indonesia said.

He added that the failure was partly due to weak cement demand as developers postponed their projects because of the May general elections. Rachmat said Gresik was likely to remain under selling pressure for the next several days.
Semen Gresik was down 275 rupiah at 4,825 rupiah, with some 2.3 million shares traded due to the poor results, brokers said.

Big-capitalised toll road operator Citra Marga was among the few gainers on talk that it was likely to take over the operation of some lucrative inner city toll roads from state-owned Jasa Marga, brokers said.
Citra Marga rose 50 rupiah to 1,375 rupiah, with some 8.8 million shares traded.
Second-liner Bakrieland rose 25 rupiah to 1,600 rupiah following announcement of a rights issue, brokers said.
